2abc6b757313f2b4c868fa2c960b7a06d7cab880.summary: KSI Digital analysed 'Ancient', a Linux IoT botnet with a custom ANCT C2 protocol, captured in a Telnet/SSH honeypot in October 2026. Devices are infected via Telnet logins and fetch a shell dropper in three versions that adds cron and init persistence. The C2 lookup is hidden inside DNS-over-TLS, and the bot stays idle while traced. A 10-minute controlled contact confirmed the C2 live. The report also covers a Mirai kit delivered from the same loader routine, and publishes indicators and detection rules.

2a4d8e3c95b83ec8a144bbd4dd83203276b21a2c.summary: Positive Technologies' PT Expert Security Center names a new threat actor, Space Pirates, active since no later than 2017. Its targets are government bodies and aerospace firms, mostly in Russia, plus Georgia and Mongolia, with some attacks on Chinese finance firms. The report describes its backdoors and loaders, including MyKLoadClient, Zupdax, RtlShare, BH_A006 and Deed RAT, and its tooling overlaps with Winnti, Bronze Union, TA428 and others. Attribution to a known group is hedged, and the report assesses the actor as having Asian roots.

hedges: The activity could not be clearly linked to any known hacker group, so the authors gave the actor a new name.
Asian roots are an assumption based on Chinese-language use, SFX archives and PDB paths.
Compile and modification dates may have been forged.
The Space Pirates and TA428 link is only a suggestion; the report says it needs further confirmation.
Whether the activity belongs to one group or several cooperating groups needs further confirmation.
Overlap with Winnti is only partly confirmed; the indirect infrastructure links require further confirmation.
Authorship of the sample built on the Snake game code is not certain; its listed owner may not be the author.
The number of victims in Mongolia is unknown.
